title: I can't believe it's taken LinkedIn so long to push back against AI slop — but will its changes really…
excerpt: LinkedIn is finally calling out AI slop for what it is
content_html:
LinkedIn, one of the most notorious bastions of AI slop online today, is finally cracking down on the deluge being seen across its site.

The social network is introducing a range of controls as it looks to turn off the tap of the torrent of AI slop increasingly dominating its website. You can try it now - just click on the three dots at the top-right of any LinkedIn post, and among the usual options to save, share or embed, you'll see a new option - "Seems like AI slop".

My only question is - what took you so long?

"We really care about this"

In a LinkedIn post of his own, Hari Srinivasan, CPO at the company, explained the reasoning behind the roll-out in words which should be music to the ears of most LinkedIn users.

"AI slop is a top priority for all of us. We really care about this," he declared. "People come to LinkedIn to connect with real people and share their real perspectives, ideas and expertise."

Now, I try and keep my LinkedIn feed fairly professional - like many of us, I do try and use it for work purposes, after all. But the odd slop does slip in every now and then - usually 3rd-level connections trying to shill some crypto scam, or religious-themed pep talk.

I have to say, it's incredibly satisfying to click the "Seems like AI slop' and relegate such posts to the dustbin of history - much more so than LinkedIn's previous system of reporting posts which may have sounded like scams or spam, but often just disappeared into silence.

As Srinivasan explained on the new reporting tools, "Slop is hard to define and the definition changes; this lets us tune our models and make better feeds."

"We asked ourselves why do people post with AI anyway? The answer is LinkedIn isn’t a one-word kind of place and they feel more confident running their posts through AI. We’re taking this learning, removing the ‘enhance your post’ feature you see when you write a post or message & replacing with a feature that proofreads your words, but does not change your voice."

Hopefully they more we use the tool, the smarter it will get - and cut down on the stuff we don't want to see. The action goes two ways though - and LinkedIn will also be testing a way for admins and members to see in their analytics dashboard when your own content has been flagged as potential slop.

Let's hope this is a bit more regulated - we don't want online vigilantes carrying out campaigns against a company or person they may have a vendetta against.

Srinivasan says the approach is based on two learnings - "First, AI and slop are not the same thing; many people refine thoughts with AI, and we believe they want to know when they sound inauthentic. Second, we want members to get feedback from real humans on what sounds authentic - not just have an AI detector review it and get it wrong."

Srinivasan also noted that LinkedIn (which let us remember is owned by Microsoft) will "continue to improve and invest in our automation defences..on comments alone, everyday we are now catching hundreds of thousands of automated comment attempts, and have blocked billions of other automation attempts (posting at scale, slop) in the last couple months alone."

This is a very welcome first step by LinkedIn, and lets just hope it's the start of an ongoing crusade against AI slop - because no one wants to see any of that anymore.

content_html_zh:
LinkedIn 是当今网上最臭名昭著的人工智能堡垒之一，它终于开始打击其网站上出现的泛滥现象。

该社交网络正在引入一系列控制措施，以期关闭日益主导其网站的人工智能洪流。 您现在就可以尝试 - 只需单击任何 LinkedIn 帖子右上角的三个点，在保存、共享或嵌入的常用选项中，您会看到一个新选项 - “看起来像 AI slop”。

我唯一的问题是 - 是什么让你花了这么长时间？

“我们真的很关心这个”

该公司首席产品官 Hari Srinivasan 在自己的 LinkedIn 帖子中解释了推出该产品背后的原因，这对大多数 LinkedIn 用户来说应该是美妙的。

“人工智能问题是我们所有人的首要任务。 我们真的很关心这个，”他宣称。 “人们来到 LinkedIn 是为了与真实的人联系并分享他们的真实观点、想法和专业知识。”

现在，我尝试让我的 LinkedIn feed 保持相当专业——毕竟，像我们许多人一样，我确实尝试将其用于工作目的。 但奇怪的事情确实会时不时地出现——通常是第三层连接试图推销一些加密货币骗局，或宗教主题的鼓舞人心的谈话。

我不得不说，点击“看起来像 AI 垃圾”并将此类帖子扔进历史垃圾箱是令人难以置信的满足 - 比 LinkedIn 以前的举报帖子系统要好得多，这些帖子可能听起来像是骗局或垃圾邮件，但通常只是消失在沉默中。

订阅 TechRadar Pro 时事通讯，获取您的企业成功所需的所有热门新闻、观点、功能和指导！

正如斯里尼瓦桑 (Srinivasan) 对新报告工具所解释的那样，“坡度很难定义，并且定义会发生变化；这让我们能够调整模型并提供更好的反馈。”

“我们问自己，为什么人们还是用人工智能发帖？ 答案是 LinkedIn 不是一个单一单词的地方，他们对通过人工智能发布帖子感到更有信心。 我们正在吸取这一教训，删除您在撰写帖子或消息时看到的‘增强您的帖子’功能，并代之以校对您的文字但不会改变您的声音的功能。”

希望我们越多地使用该工具，它就会变得越聪明，并减少我们不想看到的东西。 不过，该行动有两种方式，LinkedIn 还将测试一种方式，让管理员和会员可以在自己的内容被标记为潜在溢出物时在他们的分析仪表板中看到。

我们希望这能受到更多监管——我们不希望网络治安维护者针对他们可能有仇的公司或个人开展活动。

斯里尼瓦桑表示，这种方法基于两个经验：“首先，人工智能和 slop 不是一回事；许多人用人工智能提炼思想，我们相信他们想知道什么时候听起来不真实。 其次，我们希望会员能够从真实的人类那里获得关于听起来真实的反馈——而不仅仅是让人工智能探测器对其进行审查并出错。”

斯里尼瓦桑还指出，LinkedIn（让我们记住它是微软旗下的）将“继续改进和投资我们的自动化防御……仅在评论方面，我们现在每天都会捕获数十万条自动评论尝试，并且仅在过去几个月就阻止了数十亿次其他自动化尝试（大规模发布、倾斜）。”

这是 LinkedIn 非常受欢迎的第一步，我们只希望这是一场针对人工智能滥用的持续斗争的开始——因为没有人想再看到这样的事情了。
